nodes.description: Reduced effective EDN1 ligand is the proposed functional consequence of disease alleles. Lys91Glu alters a furin recognition motif and Pro77His lies near the ECE cleavage region. Functional evidence from different substitutions supports this model but cannot quantify residual activity of these ACS alleles.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in endothelin 1 cause recessive auriculocondylar syndrome and dominant isolated question-mark ears.
evidence.snippet: The different mode of inheritance for the F1 and S1 mutant EDN1 alleles compared to the F2 and F3 alleles might be explained by differences in the amount of residual functional protein in each case.

nodes.description: DLX5 and DLX6 transcripts were reduced in four postnatal ACS mandibular-osteoblast cultures relative to calvarial controls. Mouse developmental experiments support the importance of the EDNRA-DLX program, but the patient assay is not a direct measurement of fetal neural-crest transcription.

evidence.reference_title: A human homeotic transformation resulting from mutations in PLCB4 and GNAI3 causes auriculocondylar syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Using quantitative, real-time RT-PCR of steady-state mRNA, we identified a 6-fold reduction of DLX5 (p < 0.005; probands versus controls) and an 8-fold reduction of DLX6 expression (p < 0.001) in mandibular osteoblasts from selective probands relative to 17 randomly selected calvarial osteoblasts from controls.

experimental_models.description: RT-qPCR detects lower DLX transcript abundance in the patient cultures.
experimental_models.name: ACS patient mandibular osteoblast cultures

nodes.description: EDN1-stimulated DAG-sensor translocation and BRET are reduced by tested PLCB4 variants in HEK293T cells. Introducing Pro838Ala at the Gq-interaction interface in cis with Arg621His attenuates its dominant interference. These are cell-based pathway readouts, not purified-enzyme kinetics; substrate trapping and altered GAP activity remain untested explanations.

evidence.reference_title: Auriculocondylar syndrome 2 results from the dominant-negative action of PLCB4 variants.
evidence.snippet: These results illustrate that PLCB4 p.Arg621His interferes with PLCB activity even when it is expressed at a sub-stoichiometric level relative to wild-type PLCB4, exemplifying a characteristic of a dominant-negative protein.

experimental_models.description: Patient-associated substitutions attenuate pathway output and interface disruption reduces interference.
experimental_models.name: PLCB4-variant DAG and transcriptional reporter assays

nodes.description: EDNRA preferentially activates Gq in the tested heterologous system. Disease-associated GNAI3 proteins suppress that response while leaving the weak Gi3 response largely unchanged under the same conditions. Normal GNAI3 is therefore not represented as an obligatory positive intermediate between EDNRA and PLCB4.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant-negative Gα subunits are a mechanism of dysregulated heterotrimeric G protein signaling in human disease.
evidence.snippet: We found that expression of any of the five ACS-associated Gαi3 mutants decreased Gq activation upon ET-1 stimulation ~65 to 85% (Fig. 6D).

experimental_models.description: BRET measures reduced Gq activation after ET-1 stimulation.
experimental_models.name: GNAI3-variant signaling in HEK293T cells

nodes.description: Patient-derived iNCC cultures have reduced 24-hour scratch closure without a detected cell-cycle distribution change. Positional identity and developmental stage of these induced cells require further characterization; reduced embryonic neural-crest colonization remains a hypothesis.

nodes.description: Mesenchymal-like cells differentiated from the same iPSC neural-crest cultures show reduced day-9 ALP activity and a modest reduction in mineralization after osteogenic induction. TWIST1 and RUNX2 expression did not significantly differ during the tested osteogenic interval.

nodes.description: iPSCs from three affected members of one family and three controls were differentiated toward neural crest. Patient cultures showed increased TWIST1 and HDAC9 mRNA and reduced 24-hour scratch closure without a detected cell-cycle distribution difference.

nodes.description: Congenital or progressive mandibular fusion can restrict mouth opening. The original selected severe cases had variable fusion to the skull base; this does not imply that all condylar hypoplasia progresses to ankylosis.

evidence.reference_title: A human homeotic transformation resulting from mutations in PLCB4 and GNAI3 causes auriculocondylar syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In each case, mandibular ankylosis was progressive, of variable severity, and characterized by inconsistent fusion to the medial and lateral pterygoid plates.

nodes.description: Selected ankylosis or severe joint dysfunction may require arthroplasty and reconstruction by an experienced craniofacial team. Procedures and graft choice are guided by anatomy and growth; comparative long-term outcomes are limited.

evidence.snippet: Craniofacial CT imaging demonstrated a small mandible and bilateral TMJ ankylosis that benefited from arthroplasty and costo- chondral grafts at 4 years of age

nodes.description: Mandibular and tongue abnormalities can narrow the oropharyngeal airway. This mechanical branch explains obstructive respiratory complications in selected patients; persistent central apnea requires separate assessment.

evidence.reference_title: Auriculocondylar syndrome 2 caused by a novel PLCB4 variant in a male Chinese neonate: A case report and review of the literature.
evidence.snippet: Computed tomography (CT) revealed a narrowed oropharynx airway and absent condylar fossae, shortened mandibular rami, and obtuse mandibular angles (Figure 2).

nodes.description: Mutants show hypoplastic lower-jaw skeletal elements and fusion across arch joints. Genetic interaction supports a conserved endothelin-phospholipase pathway.
